rows.q: 量子力学里的虚数单位 i 从何而来？
rows.answer: 在最底层的元胞动力学中本无虚数单位 i。只要取定恰当的实正交基底，描述单个元胞演化的哈密顿矩阵全部分量均为实数。i 并非人为引入，而是几何循环的自然产物：元胞的四个顶点首尾相连形成一条闭合回路，回路上最自然的对称操作便是将各顶点状态顺序轮转一格。连续轮转四次恰好回到初始构型；因而在该循环操作所激发的二维非平庸平面上，轮转一格恰好代表旋转四分之一圈（90°）。四分之一圈具备一项直观性质：连续旋转两次便相当于旋转 180° 并反向，在代数上即等于乘以 −1。任何连续作用两次等价于乘以 −1 的算符，本身便实现了 −1 的平方根——这正是 i。它既非外加假设，亦未硬编码入运动方程，而是在回路闭合时自然涌现的相位规则：每推进一格乘以 i，走满四步正好复原。就单一元胞而言，这一步的代数表示论严格闭合；真正尚未闭合的是最后一步：认定这一局域的四分之一圈复结构正是整个物理网络所共有、并主宰全局量子演化的同一个 i。
rows.rides: 依赖该定理自身的条件性部分：即认定这一局域四分之一圈循环算符便是驱动全局动力学、为整张网络所共有的那个统一虚数单位 i。至于由离散循环推出满足 i² = −1 的那一半表示论证明，已完全闭合，不依赖任何开放接口。
rows.check: 《实真空》一章“K4 上 i 的涌现：三种成分”及其表示引理；闭合回路论证段落；数值验证见实验 074（虚数单位的 Z₄ 定位）。专著中将该定理表述在由四个元胞拼成的闭合方格环上，而数值证书与自举定理则直接采用单个元胞的四个顶点，二者代数结构严格同构。机器端已完成标量四次方根核心与 2 × 2 矩阵块的 Lean 核验。
rows.lead: 虚数单位 i 并非预先写入方程：绕该对象四个顶点构成的闭合回路前进两步，即精确落于 −1。

rows.q: 标准模型中的电荷为何偏偏呈现那组奇异分数？
rows.answer: 标准模型的每一代物质粒子，连同希格斯玻色子与右手中微子，共包含七类基础场。每一类场携带一项称为弱超荷的量子数，再结合弱同位旋即可定出其电荷：电子的 −1 与上夸克的 +2/3 皆由此得来。若直接列举，这七个弱超荷呈现为一串令人费解的分数：1/6、2/3、−1/3、−1/2、−1、0、1/2。但若将它们统统乘以 6，便立即化为一串整齐整数：(1, 4, −2, −3, −6, 0, 3)。若将四面体元胞首尾连接构成闭合环路，环路自身的离散几何便自然生成一把具有七道刻度的整数标尺，范围为 −2 至 +4（在此机制下，7 个刻度已被证明是能闭合成环的最小格点数）。其中五个整数恰好与标准模型的五个乘六弱超荷（−2、0、+1、+3、+4）直接重合；另外两个起始位置（−1 与 +2）恰好落在元胞拼接的边界界面上，对应于两类带电轻子行。几何约束在此处留下一项联合自由度：该界面上的两行必须同向平移同一整数 δ。平移量 δ 究竟取何值？教科书中的标准自洽条件立即给出唯一解：首先，手征反常必须精确相消（各行量子效应之和必须严格归零，否则理论自相矛盾）——唯一确定 δ = −5；其次，中微子必须能通过希格斯机制获得质量——同样唯一给出 −5；最后，电子也须由希格斯场赋予质量——该条件约束两者同步移动。因此 δ = −5：界面上的 −1 平移为 −6，+2 平移为 −3，恰好精准复现标准模型的两项轻子弱超荷数值（这两项已移出原有七格标尺之外）。整个推演过程从未提前填入任何粒子名称，所有名字——夸克双重态、上、下、轻子双重态、电子、右手中微子、希格斯——全都是得出整数序列后方才对应的物理标签。而断言这七行匿名整数正对应于时空中的七类物理粒子，已被作者列为开放步骤。
rows.rides: 七行整数序列本身不含任何粒子标签。将该匿名序列正式对应至标准模型每一代的七类场（含希格斯场与右手中微子），属于作者自己标注的开放接口（E8）。整数序列的唯一性并不依赖该接口。
rows.check: 《多元胞》一章“带类型标准模型乘积的匿名载体唯一性”定理；迫使 δ = −5 的手征反常敷层定理（证明中明示：前两项物理自洽条件各自独立定出 −5，第三项仅锁定同步偏移）；“最小七格格点”定理；P2P/F2F 物种分类引理。详见审阅问题 8。
rows.lead: 标准模型那七个看似古怪的弱超荷分数，同乘以 6 后皆化为整数；这串整数正是由元胞环路几何与反常相消共同逼出的唯一解。

rows.scale: 10⁻¹⁵ m · 中子与强 CP 问题
rows.q: 强相互作用为什么不破坏 CP 对称？又为什么不需要轴子？
rows.answer: 强相互作用（QCD）理论中原本天然带有一个称为 θ 角的参数，原则上可以在 0° 至 360° 之间任意取值。该参数直接控制着强相互作用是否破坏 CP 对称（粒子—反粒子共轭与空间反演联合对称）：只要 θ 显著偏离零，中子便会呈现可观测的电偶极矩。然而实验长期精确测得该角度小于百亿分之一圈。学术界主流解释是引入一种假想新粒子——轴子（axion），充当动力学势能机制将 θ 角拉回零点；但历经四十余年搜寻仍未发现其踪迹。在本框架内，则无需额外引入轴子。核心道理极为简明：正四面体在镜面反射下仍是自身，仅相当于交换两个顶点的编号；而顶点编号纯属冗余标记，不影响物理实质，却会反转真空缠绕的拓扑取向，相当于将 θ 变为 −θ。在离散镜像约束下，一个满足 θ = −θ（模 2π）的角度仅有 0° 与 180° 两种离散可能：原本连续可调的 θ 参数实际上只是一个双态开关。进一步结合本框架选定的“实真空分支”（在恰当基底下其耦合矩阵完全不含虚数 i），开关只能锁定在 θ = 0° 这一闭合位置。这一保护机制内生于四面体对称性，而非事后强加。至于物理观测角中另一项来源于夸克质量矩阵复相位的贡献，亦由另一项独立论证予以消除。此处需明确说明两点：其一，弱相互作用中的 CP 破坏（如 K 介子与 B 介子衰变中的现象）并未受此消去，依然保留；其二，实验迄今对中子电偶极矩与轴子耦合仅给出上限，故本结论的现行科学状态是“尚未被证伪”，而非“已被证实”。若未来实验确实探测到解决强 CP 问题所需的 QCD 轴子，本框架选定的真空分支即告证伪。BabyIAXO 轴子望远镜当前计划约于 2029 年安装磁体、2030 年后调试运行（具体进度仍视工程安排而定）。
rows.rides: 依赖框架所选定的实真空分支假设，并辅以对夸克质量矩阵复相位及量子辐射修正稳定性的另一独立闭环论证。在实验检验层面仅存在单边上限：落在所有现有上限之下仅代表尚未触及检验阈值，绝非已被实验确认。
rows.check: 《K4 元胞》一章“θ_QCD 的拓扑禁戒”，配以由量子几何张量厄米性导出的强 CP 定理；《实真空》一章“真空为实 ⇒ θ = 0”推论与“无需引入轴子”推论；《预言》一章分支选择检验 1（IAXO、ALPHA）。
rows.lead: 四面体在镜像反演下保持自身对称，从而使强作用 CP 参数仅余离散开关选择，在实真空分支上自动锁定为零，无需引入轴子。

rows.scale: 全尺度 · 引力与规范力
rows.q: 引力与规范力，为什么可视为同一块几何的双面？
rows.answer: 试设想在球面上沿闭合路径环行一周并回到起点，途中随身携带两台测量仪器：一台计步器记录走过的几何路程，一台傅科摆记录方向基准。归来时，尽管途中从未触碰过摆锤，其摆动平面却偏转了一个几何角度——计步器读取的是空间度规（距离），而傅科摆读取的则是平行移动带来的曲率（几何相位）。当这一 K₄ 量子基态在自身耦合参数构成的控制空间中迁移时，同样随身带着这两面几何结构：它们并非两套互不相关的物理组件，而是同一复值对象——量子几何张量（Quantum Geometric Tensor，Provost–Vallée, 1980）——的实部与虚部。本理论的独特之处不在于这一经典拆分，而在于在这仅含 81 个基态的有限模型上将两面一并推算到底。张量的实部（对称部分）刻画两个邻近量子态之间的可分辨距离，表现为时空度规——引力便由实部给出；张量的虚部（反对称部分，即 Berry 曲率）刻画内部量子态箭头沿闭合回路平行移动一周后的相位偏转，表现为规范场强——强、弱与电磁相互作用的杨–米尔斯型场皆由虚部给出。这两面同出于同一量子几何张量，在有限系统内已是闭合定理。框架更进一步押下的物理学赌注则是：二者的动力学方程亦同源导出，即爱因斯坦引力场方程与杨–米尔斯方程出自同一变分源头，而非人为拼合。该动力学步被明确表述为一组附带完整前提条件的场方程系统；为此拆分独立投稿的专题论文标题即为《条件性爱因斯坦–杨–米尔斯场方程》。
rows.rides:
将该双面张量转化为条件性动力学场方程的一步，依赖作者列出的四项开放因素：
- 从底层基底向电弱作用（弱力与电磁力）的规范提升尚未闭合（E3）。
- 如何由四个完全对称的欧氏方向过渡为 3+1 维洛伦兹时空，以及引力基底如何自零构造而非仅作分类（E7）。
- 对应于引力波的无质量自旋为二传播激发态尚未构造完成（E11）。
- 响应展开中的高阶修正塔：现有推导仅给出领头阶方程系统，此项高阶截断暂未另设独立编号。
而“度规与规范曲率同出于同一量子几何张量”这一步本身不依赖任何开放接口。
rows.check: 《Grassmann 流形》一章：量子几何张量（Provost–Vallée, 1980）的对称/反对称正交拆分及其反对称引理；Einstein–Yang–Mills 基底方程（专著中相应章节的限定词已通过勘误 E4 收窄）；由此拆分的独立专题论文《条件性 Einstein–Yang–Mills 场方程》已完成修订，正准备改投其他期刊。相关审阅问题见 1 与 2。
rows.lead: 同一复量子几何张量包含实部与虚部两面：引力度规由实部给出，规范相互作用曲率由虚部给出。

rows.q: Where does the imaginary unit of quantum mechanics come from?
rows.answer: Down in the engine that runs the universe there is no i: written in the right basis, the table of numbers that runs one cell is real through and through. The i comes from geometry. The cell’s four corners close into a loop, and the loop has one natural move — shift everything one corner along. Four shifts bring you home, so on the part of the pattern this move actually rotates, one shift is a quarter turn. A quarter turn has a property you can check on a steering wheel: do it twice and you have turned around, which is multiplication by −1. Anything that squares to −1 is, by definition, i. It was never written into the equations; it appears once the loop is closed, each step multiplying by i and four steps bringing you back to the start. What is closed is the mathematics of that step. What the author leaves open is the last stretch: that this local quarter turn is the one i that drives the dynamics and is shared by the whole network.
rows.rides: The theorem’s own conditional half: that the local quarter turn is the one i that drives the dynamics and is shared by the whole network. The representation half — that the shift really does act as a quarter turn, one that squares to −1 — is closed and rides on no interface.
rows.check: “Emergence of i on K4 from three ingredients” and its Representation Lemma, real-vacuum chapter; the loop-closing passage; Experiment 074, the Z₄ location of the imaginary unit. The monograph states the theorem for a closed square of four cells; the numerical certificate and the bootstrap theorem use the four corners (sites) of one cell; the algebra is the same. Machine side: the scalar fourth-root core and the 2 × 2 block.
rows.lead: i was not written into the equations. Walk two steps round the object’s four corners and you land exactly on −1.

rows.q: Why are the charges the odd fractions they are?
rows.answer: Each generation of Standard-Model matter, together with the Higgs and a right-handed neutrino, has seven kinds of field. Each carries a number called hypercharge; combine it with weak isospin and out comes the electric charge: the electron’s −1, the up quark’s +2/3. The seven are an odd list of fractions: 1/6, 2/3, −1/3, −1/2, −1, 0, 1/2. Multiply them by 6 and they become (1, 4, −2, −3, −6, 0, 3), every one an integer. Glue tetrahedral cells into a closed ring and the ring’s geometry produces an integer ruler of its own with exactly seven marks, −2 to +4; within this mechanism, seven is provably the fewest. Five marks match five of those integers directly: −2, 0, +1, +3, +4. The other two, −1 and +2, are where the two charged leptons start; they sit on the seams where cells are glued, and the geometry says only one thing about them — both must shift, and by the same integer. By how much? The rules are the textbook ones. The anomaly must cancel (a quantum effect that has to cancel exactly across the seven rows, or the theory contradicts itself): that demands −5. The neutrino must be able to get a mass from the Higgs: that demands −5 as well. The electron’s mass term fixes no number, only that both leptons shift alike. So δ = −5: −1 becomes −6 and +2 becomes −3, the Standard Model’s two lepton values, both now outside the seven-mark ruler. No particle name enters anywhere; the names — quark doublet, up, down, lepton doublet, electron, right-handed neutrino, Higgs — are labels attached at the end. That these seven rows of numbers are the seven kinds of particle in spacetime is a step the author himself lists as open.
rows.rides: Matching the seven anonymous rows — seven numbers with no particle names attached — to the Standard Model’s seven kinds of field (Higgs and right-handed neutrino included) is an interface the author himself lists as open (E8). The integers do not depend on it.

Review Target 8.
rows.lead: Multiply the Standard Model’s seven odd charge fractions by six and every one is a whole number — and the geometry forces exactly that list.

rows.q: Why does the strong force show no CP violation, and why is no axion needed?
rows.answer: The theory of the strong force comes with an angle, θ, that could in principle be anything from 0 to 360 degrees: a dial. θ governs CP symmetry — swap every particle for its antiparticle, look in a mirror, and ask whether the laws still read the same. If θ is not zero the neutron becomes a tiny battery, one end positive and one negative; experiment says the angle is under one ten-billionth of a full turn. The standard answer brings in another particle, the axion, a spring that pulls the dial back to zero; forty years of searching has not found it. Here no spring is needed. A tetrahedron in a mirror is still a tetrahedron with two corners swapped, and the corner labels were never physical, so swapping them changes no physics — yet it reverses the direction of every knot the vacuum can tie, turning θ into −θ. An angle equal to its own negative has two options, 0 or 180 degrees: the dial was a switch all along. The switch sits on “off” because the vacuum branch this framework selects is the real one: in the right basis its table of numbers carries no i at all. The symmetry is not added by hand; it is the tetrahedron’s own. The angle’s other half, hidden in the phase of the quark masses, is switched off by a separate argument. Two things to be clear about: the CP violation of the weak force — the kind seen in kaon and B-meson decays — is not erased along with it; and experiment so far gives only an upper limit, so this claim is “not yet refuted”, not “confirmed”. A detected axion of the kind the strong force would need (a QCD axion) would put the world outside this branch. BabyIAXO’s current plan puts magnet installation around 2029, followed by commissioning and axion runs from 2030 onward; the schedule may move.
rows.rides: The choice of the real-vacuum branch. The other half of the physical angle — the phase of the quark masses — and its stability under quantum corrections are closed by a separate argument of their own. On the comparison side this is a bound: below every current limit means untested, not confirmed.
rows.check: “Topological prohibition of θ_QCD”, K4-cell chapter, with the quantum-geometric-tensor Hermiticity strong-CP theorem; the real-vacuum chapter’s corollaries “real vacuum ⇒ θ = 0” and “no axion required”; branch-selection Test 1 in the predictions chapter (IAXO, ALPHA).
rows.lead: A tetrahedron in a mirror is still a tetrahedron, so the dial that could break CP can only sit at zero: no new particle needed.

rows.scale: every scale · gravity and the gauge forces
rows.q: Why are gravity and the gauge forces one geometry read twice?
rows.answer: Imagine walking a closed loop on a sphere carrying two instruments. A pedometer records how far you walked. A Foucault pendulum that was swinging north when you set out is found, on your return, swinging in a different plane, though you never touched it. The pedometer reads distance; the pendulum reads “came back to the same place, yet turned”. When this object’s quantum ground state walks through its “settings space” (the values of its couplings), it carries both instruments too — not two things but two faces of one geometry, packed into a single complex number: real part the pedometer, imaginary part the pendulum. That number is the quantum geometric tensor (Provost and Vallée, 1980). What is new here is not the split but following both faces to the end on one finite object of 81 states. The real face measures how distinguishable two states are and reads as distance, a metric: gravity lives on this face. The imaginary face measures how far an internal arrow turns when carried round a loop and reads as curvature: the Yang–Mills-type fields that describe the strong, weak and electromagnetic forces live on this face. That both faces come off one tensor is a theorem. The bet this framework places is the next step: that their dynamics therefore arrive together, Einstein’s equations and the Yang–Mills equations from one source rather than glued side by side. That step is written as a conditional system with its conditions listed one by one; the paper drawn from it is titled “Conditional Einstein–Yang–Mills Field Equations”.
rows.rides:
The step written as a conditional system rides on four things the author lists as open:
- The step up to the weak and electromagnetic forces (E3).
- The passage from a geometry with four alike directions to three of space and one of time, together with the most basic piece of gravity, which is classified rather than built (E7).
- The massless spin-two excitation that gravitational waves are made of, not yet constructed (E11).
- A tower of higher-order response terms: what is derived is the leading system only. This one carries no interface number of its own.
The step that both faces come off one tensor rides on no interface.
rows.check: The symmetric/antisymmetric split of the quantum geometric tensor (Provost and Vallée, 1980) and its antisymmetry lemma, Grassmannian chapter; the Einstein–Yang–Mills substrate equations, whose title qualifier in the monograph is narrowed by erratum E4; the standalone conditional Einstein–Yang–Mills paper has completed revision and is being prepared for submission to a new journal. Review Targets 1 and 2.
rows.lead: One geometry with two faces: gravity is read off one of them, the other forces off the other.

imaginary.title: Where the imaginary unit comes from
imaginary.aTitle: A real engine, a closed loop
imaginary.aSub: Start from a real substrate and the real, symmetric table of numbers that runs it (a Hamiltonian) — no i anywhere.
imaginary.aNote: Dashed: the cell’s other two links, which this loop does not use. Every step multiplies the accumulated phase — the angle it has turned through — by i once more; four steps bring it back to +1.
imaginary.closeLabel: fourth step, back to +1: the loop closes, and a full circuit carries no phase at all
imaginary.bTitle: The cell’s clock: a rotation by 2π/n
imaginary.bSub: The unit must be a genuine complex structure — it must really square to −1.
imaginary.verdictOk: A quarter turn: its square lands exactly on −1
imaginary.verdictNo: A third of a turn: its square misses −1 by 60°
imaginary.bNote: A quarter turn squares to −1; a third of a turn does not. So n = 4. Machine side: a companion module rules out every n ≥ 5 by a different count.
imaginary.caption: The engine is real: written in the right basis, the table of numbers that runs one cell has no i in it. The i is walked into existence — the cell’s four corners close into a loop, each step multiplies by i, and four steps bring you back to the start. In the author’s words: “complex quantum mechanics is the geometric price of closing a two-dimensional loop.” That unit is the cell’s clock, a rotation by 2π/n; a quarter turn squares to −1 and a third of a turn does not, so n = 4, which is also why the object has four corners.
imaginary.ridesOn: The theorem’s own conditional half: that this local quarter turn is the one i that drives the dynamics and is shared by the whole network. The representation half — that the shift really does act as a quarter turn — is closed.

The monograph states the theorem for a closed square of four cells; the numerical certificate and the bootstrap theorem use the four corners (sites) of one cell; the algebra is the same. hypercharge.title: Seven fractions, times six
hypercharge.intNoteB: each of two independent conditions fixes it
hypercharge.note: The seven rows are the seven kinds of field in one generation, Higgs and right-handed neutrino included. Five integers sit directly on the ring’s seven-mark ruler; the other two come from the two remaining marks (−1 and +2), shifted together by −5, a number fixed twice over by two independent conditions, with a third condition requiring only that both shift alike. The shifted −3 and −6 lie outside the seven marks.
hypercharge.caption: Multiply the Standard Model’s seven hypercharges by six and you get the list the ring’s seven anonymous rows are forced to, in order. The integers come from anomaly cancellation together with one integer lift, {delta}; two independent conditions each fix that value, and a third requires only that both lepton rows shift alike. The names are set in grey and a break separates them from the arithmetic: they are attached afterwards, and no equation in the derivation uses them.
